learn.pageTitle: Riichi Mahjong Scoring for Closed Hands Other Than Pinfu
learn.pageDescription: How to score a closed standard hand that is not pinfu in riichi mahjong. Add the 20 base fu, the fu for ron or tsumo and the fu you built up, then round up to the next 10. This lesson shows where the fu typically round up (tenpane), for ron and tsumo separately.
learn.startTitle: A closed ron other than pinfu is never 30 fu
learn.startBody1:
We covered [[chiitoitsu|chiitoitsu]] and [[pinfu|pinfu]] first because they are the two exceptions that do not build up fu.
From here on we look at hands that do build up fu: [[menzen|closed]] [[mentsute|standard hands]] other than pinfu.
learn.startBody2:
When you [[hora|win]] a closed standard hand by [[ron|ron]], the 10 fu [[menzen-ron-kafu|closed ron bonus]] goes on top of the 20 [[futei|base fu]], so you start from 30 fu.
And from there, the [[mentsu|sets]], the [[jantou|pair]] or the [[machi|wait]] are sure to add some fu.
learn.startBody3:
If every set is a [[shuntsu|sequence]], the pair is not [[yakuhai|yakuhai]] and the wait is [[ryanmen|two-sided]], a closed standard hand with all three is pinfu as it stands.
In other words, a closed standard hand that is not pinfu always builds up some fu.
learn.startBody4:
So a closed standard hand that is not pinfu is always 40 fu or more on a ron. Put the other way round, the only closed 30 fu ron is pinfu.
[[tsumo|Tsumo]], on the other hand, starts from 22 fu (the 20 base fu plus 2 fu for tsumo), so after rounding up its minimum is 30 fu.
learn.roundTitle: Where the fu typically round up
learn.roundBody1:
The fu of a standard hand are the 20 base fu, the fu for how you won (10 fu for a closed ron, 2 fu for tsumo) and all the fu built up by the sets, the pair and the wait, added together and rounded up to the next 10 fu.
You count the built-up fu just as in the <mentsuLink></mentsuLink>, <jantouLink></jantouLink> and <machiLink></machiLink> lessons.
learn.roundBody2:
When the total has a remainder in the ones place and is carried up to the next 10 fu, this is called “tenpane”.
Every fu value is a multiple of 2, so the total always rounds up unless it happens to be an exact multiple of 10. Ron and tsumo start from different points, so we look at where the total rounds up for each one separately.
learn.ronTitle: Ron (from 30 fu: 20 base fu + 10 fu closed ron bonus)
learn.ronNote:
The starting point of 30 fu is already a multiple of 10, so a single source of fu is enough to make the total round up.
The only time you avoid rounding up is when the built-up fu add up to an exact multiple of 10.
learn.tsumoTitle: Tsumo (from 22 fu: 20 base fu + 2 fu for tsumo)
learn.tsumoNote:
Because of the 2 fu for tsumo, the totals that come out exact are shifted by 2 fu from ron. If the built-up fu are 8, 18 and so on, the total is exact; if they are 10, 20 and so on, it rounds up.
A single closed triplet of terminals or honors (8 fu) on its own keeps the hand at 30 fu. It is not “a closed triplet means 40 fu”: the hand goes up to 40 fu only when 2 fu for the wait or the pair are added on top, making 32 fu, which rounds up.
